title: 4GE1-style exam questions: The hydrological cycle and drainage basins (1.1)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y10 lesson 53 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 53: The hydrological cycle and drainage basins (1.1). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Draw and annotate a drainage basin system diagram with inputs, stores, transfers and outputs.
questions.a: Labelled diagram with precipitation input; interception, soil, groundwater stores; infiltration, percolation, throughflow, runoff, groundwater flow; evaporation, transpiration and discharge outputs
questions.model: Teacher starts it: a box for 'precipitation' at the top, arrows to 'interception store' and 'surface', then 'infiltration' down to 'soil store'.

questions.q: Explain why a drainage basin is called an open system but the global hydrological cycle a closed one.
questions.a: The global cycle keeps the same total water (1); a basin gains water from precipitation and loses it by evaporation and discharge (1), so water crosses its boundary (1)

questions.q: Suggest how building a town would change water transfers in a basin.
questions.a: Impermeable surfaces reduce infiltration (1), so more surface runoff reaches the river faster (1)

questions.q: Describe what happens to rain that falls on a forested hillside.
questions.a: Some is intercepted by leaves and evaporates (1); some infiltrates the soil and moves as throughflow (1); some percolates to groundwater and slowly reaches the river (1)
questions.model: Follow the drop: first leaves (interception). Then the soil (infiltration, throughflow). Then deeper (percolation, groundwater). Each step slows the water down.

questions.a: The point where two rivers meet

questions.q: State two outputs from a drainage basin.
questions.a: Two of: evaporation, transpiration, river discharge to the sea

questions.q: Big question: where does the water in a river come from?
questions.a: Precipitation that reaches the channel by surface runoff, throughflow and groundwater flow
